proposals: The Ministry of Heavy Industries should publish a component-wise breakdown of the REPM scheme that reconciles the ₹7,280 crore headline with its ₹6,450 crore sales incentive and ₹750 crore capital subsidy, so the unexplained ₹80 crore is either identified as a line item or dropped from official statements.

The Ministry of Heavy Industries should publish the outcome of the REPM evaluation — the five selected beneficiaries, each one’s committed capacity and commissioning date, and the technical scores of all 20 bidders, so whether the awards add up to the 6,000 MTPA target can be checked.

The Ministry of Heavy Industries and the Ministry of Steel should issue a joint clarification on whether electrical steel and magnet-alloy inputs used by REPM beneficiaries can also claim under PLI 1.2, and how double claims are prevented, so integrated motor-component investors know their position before committing capital.

The Ministry of Heavy Industries should report each year REPM output, sales and incentive paid alongside DGCIS imports under HS 8505.11 and 8505.19, so the scheme’s effect on a $220.8 million import bill that was 73.0% from China in 2024–25 is measured, not assumed.
